extracted.intended_audience: researchers, authors, librarians, and readers interested in F1000's publishing and peer-review model
extracted.subtask_description: Describes F1000's model for publishing research with post-publication, public peer review and the submission/visibility requirements for content on the platform. Useful for authors considering submission or readers evaluating F1000-published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication peer review (timing of review)
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000 offers peer-review after, rather than before, publishing a research article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles are published following a prepublication check, then an expert is assigned to conduct the peer-review after publication. The model contrasts with traditional pre-publication peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and ongoing review (visibility and updateability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer-review is done publicly, online, and on an ongoing basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and any subsequent commentary are visible to readers and can continue after initial publication, enabling continuous evaluation and updates to the assessment of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity and disclosure (no anonymity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The expert conducting the peer review discloses their name and any vested interests, abandoning the double-blind, anonymous peer-review system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are named and must disclose conflicts of interest, prioritizing transparency over reviewer anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission includes underlying data
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submit an article and all of its underlying data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F1000's submission requirement expects accompanying data to be provided with the article to support openness and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepublication checks (screening prior to posting)
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000 does a prepublication check and publishes the article, usually within a couple weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before posting, F1000 performs basic checks (not full peer review) to ensure minimal standards are met; after this check the article is published quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Passed peer review' status and filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can filter articles to see only those that have passed peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F1000 tracks peer-review outcomes so readers can select content that has undergone and met peer-review standards; the platform provides filters based on review status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert selection based on importance/significance (Faculty Opinions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty Opinions experts nominated primary research papers they felt were important or interesting, wrote a description of the work's significance, then linked to where the work was originally published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and recommendation are based on expert judgment of importance/interest and on concise significance summaries rather than purely on citation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation/ranking as an alternative to citation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty Opinions drew attention to scientific works that are well-rated by F1000's experts; the Faculty Opinions ranking system provided an alternative article highlighting system from the use of article impact metrics like total citation count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert ratings and curated recommendations function as qualitative indicators of significance and may be used in lieu of or alongside quantitative citation counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted content types for publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication types: Reviews, scientific articles, posters, slides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F1000 accepts a variety of research-related content types (not limited to traditional articles), which authors can submit under the publisher's open research model.
